incident_summary: Between 2020-09-20 04:21 UTC and 2020-09-20 09:14 UTC, an external actor authenticated to DC01 over RDP using compromised domain credentials, executed a Cobalt Strike beacon staged at C:\Windows\Temp\update.exe, established Run-key persistence under svc-backup, dumped LSASS to obtain additional credentials, then pivoted via RDP to DESKTOP-SDN1RPT. Approximately 84 MB of files from the Sales share were collected and exfiltrated to 203.0.113.74 over HTTPS to drudge-report.tk before the session terminated. Cross-source corroboration across disk, memory and network confirms the attack chain end-to-end.

attack_narrative.narrative: The attacker authenticated to DC01 over RDP at 04:21 UTC using the svc-backup domain account from external IP 203.0.113.74. The account had not previously logged on interactively. Logon Type 10 events in Security.evtx confirmed the session, and the network capture corroborated TCP 3389 traffic from the same source.

The attacker spawned an encoded PowerShell command from the RDP session, which downloaded and executed update.exe — a Cobalt Strike beacon — to C:\Windows\Temp. PID 3284 was observed in the memory capture with svchost.exe parentage, masquerading consistent with named-pipe injection.

attack_narrative.mitre_technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys
attack_narrative.narrative: The attacker installed a Run-key entry under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run named WindowsUpdate, pointing to C:\Windows\Temp\update.exe, ensuring re-execution at next svc-backup logon.

The attacker dumped LSASS process memory to C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp using rundll32.exe with comsvcs.dll MiniDump. The on-disk dump matched the in-memory artifact, and the prefetch trace placed rundll32 execution within seconds of the dump file's creation timestamp.

Using svc-backup credentials harvested from LSASS, the attacker pivoted from DC01 to DESKTOP-SDN1RPT over RDP at 06:18 UTC. RDP cache bitmaps recovered from the workstation profile rendered a partial view of the attacker's desktop, and the Security.evtx on the workstation logged a Logon Type 10 originating from DC01.

The attacker enumerated and copied approximately 84 MB of files from \\DC01\Sales to a staging folder at C:\Users\svc-backup\AppData\Local\Temp\stage on DESKTOP-SDN1RPT. ShellBags entries and Jumplists confirmed the directory traversal.

The beacon communicated with drudge-report.tk over HTTPS on TCP/443 at regular jittered intervals. JA3 fingerprint 72a589da586844d7f0818ce684948eea matched a known Cobalt Strike default profile, and the destination resolved to 203.0.113.74 — the same IP used for the initial RDP session.

The attacker compressed the staged Sales data into stage.7z (84 MB) and transferred it over the existing HTTPS C2 channel between 08:51 UTC and 09:14 UTC. Bro/Zeek HTTP logs recorded a single PUT request consistent with the file size.

objectives: Establish baseline timeline of suspicious activity
operational_periods_summary.ic_reasoning: Three evidence sources delivered: DC01 disk image, DC01 memory capture, and a 4-hour PCAP. Triage runs broad first-pass to surface anomalous logons. Forensics, Memory, Network branches activated in parallel. Malware branch held — no flagged binary yet.

objectives: Determine root cause of suspicious svc-backup logon
Locate and characterize the executable referenced by Run-key persistence
Confirm whether memory PID 3284 corresponds to the Run-key target
operational_periods_summary.ic_reasoning: Triage surfaced an external RDP logon for svc-backup which has no prior interactive history. Forensics located update.exe and Run-key persistence. Memory found PID 3284. Activating Malware branch to triage the binary on disk vs in-memory image.

objectives: Resolve apparent contradiction between Prefetch evidence and in-memory image base
operational_periods_summary.ic_reasoning: Memory reported PID 3284 as the C2 process. Forensics found a Prefetch entry for update.exe with a hash that didn't match the in-memory image base on first comparison. Re-tasked Forensics: verify whether Prefetch corresponds to the same binary as PID 3284's image. Result: yes — the attacker renamed it after first execution. Contradiction resolved. Lateral movement to DESKTOP-SDN1RPT confirmed via RDP cache bitmaps.
Exfiltration confirmed via Zeek HTTP logs. JA3 fingerprint matched Cobalt Strike default. All major findings now corroborated by ≥2 sources. Documentation Unit cleared to publish final_report.json.
